links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of PathFX survival predictions in external local cohort
links.effect: Best model (18-month) AUC 0.63, Brier 0.22, calibration slope 0.58, intercept 0.21; other AUCs did not exceed 0.68; survival systematically underestimated.
links.quote: In general, the accuracy and other performance parameters we observed for PathFX were inadequate for clinical use.

links.outcome: PathFX performance differences across sex, race and treatment-period subgroups
links.effect: Better discrimination in females and poorer performance with flatter calibration slopes in patients who were not White; no clear differences by treatment period.
links.quote: The subgroup analyses suggested heterogeneity; that is, the model exhibited a better discrimination in females and poorer performance in patients who were not White with flatter calibration slopes.

links.outcome: Calibration of PathFX in local population indicating need for recalibration
links.effect: Intercepts positive at all time points (survival underestimated); slopes <1 (overconfident probabilities); recalibration or redevelopment recommended.
links.quote: Intercepts were positive for all time points, which means that the model systematically underestimated survival in this patient population.

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation and fairness evaluation of an existing clinical risk prediction tool (PathFX) across demographic subgroups, without testing an active deployment safeguard or intervention.
